themes_detail.label: Encampment surge in parks
themes_detail.summary: Homeless encampment complaints spiked to 11 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% increase (z-score: 5.57)—coinciding with repeated community board requests for enhanced park safety and security staff, suggesting a concentrated homelessness crisis in Washington Heights/Inwood parks.
evidence: 11 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly baseline (8-week average)
700% spike with z-score 5.57 (statistically significant high-severity anomaly)
Community Board has repeatedly budgeted for 'enhance park safety through more security staff' — same request year after year, suggesting chronic, now-acute problem
Park Rules violation complaints also up 700% THIS WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.4 baseline)
reporting_angles: Ground reporting: Which parks are most affected? Interview residents, Parks Dept, local advocates about why encampments are concentrating now.
Policy angle: Why have park safety funding requests been denied repeatedly? What resources exist to address homelessness in public spaces?

themes_detail.label: Bike/skate activity spike
themes_detail.summary: Bike/Roller/Skate complaints exploded to 3 complaints 3 weeks ago from a near-zero baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69, highest statistical anomaly on record)—signaling either a concentrated cycling/skating nuisance event or emerging enforcement activity.
evidence: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks = 2300% spike
Highest z-score on dataset (8.69), indicating extreme statistical rarity
Baseline was near-zero, making this a newly emergent issue type in this district
reporting_angles: What triggered the spike? Interview NYPD, Parks Enforcement, and community members about specific incidents.
Is this a one-off event or early signal of a trend? Check whether complaints have continued past 3 weeks ago.

themes_detail.label: Street cleanliness deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street Sweeping complaints jumped to 9 complaints 3 weeks ago versus 1.0 per week baseline—an 800% spike (z-score: 4.82)—paired with longstanding community board requests for 'more frequent litter basket collection,' indicating sanitation service gaps are now creating visible resident complaint surges.
evidence: 9 street sweeping complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly baseline = 800% spike (z-score: 4.82)
Community Board has consistently requested 'Provide more frequent litter basket collection' from Department of Sanitation—same request year after year
UNSANITARY CONDITION remains top 5 complaint type overall (1,376 complaints over 90 days), showing persistent baseline problem
reporting_angles: Interview Sanitation Department: What caused the service gap 3 weeks ago? Has staffing or collection schedules changed?
Community impact: Walk affected streets, photograph conditions, talk to residents and local business owners about cleanliness complaints.

themes_detail.label: Graffiti vandalism cluster
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 4 complaints 3 weeks ago from a 0.6 per week baseline—a 540% increase (z-score: 4.85)—suggesting a concentrated vandalism event or outbreak in the district that may signal broader public space security concerns.
evidence: 4 graffiti complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly baseline = 540% spike (z-score: 4.85)
Concurrent with Street Sweeping spike and Encampment spike, suggesting broader public space degradation 3 weeks ago
Community Board budget requests include interest in park safety and facilities upgrades, indicating quality-of-life concerns
reporting_angles: Geographic mapping: Which streets/areas saw the graffiti spike? Are they concentrated near parks or transit hubs?
Enforcement response: Did NYPD or Sanitation escalate removal efforts? How quickly was vandalism addressed?

themes_detail.label: SPIT enforcement activity uptick
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team complaints rose to 4 complaints last week from 0.8 per week baseline—a 433% spike (z-score: 3.92)—possibly reflecting heightened code enforcement or compliance issues in housing, construction, or building safety.
evidence: 4 SPIT complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly baseline = 433% spike (z-score: 3.92)
380 total DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (330 alterations), suggesting active construction/renovation environment where SPIT inspections would increase
Housing Authority has repeated budget requests for 'Install security cameras or make other safety upgrades,' hinting at ongoing building quality concerns
reporting_angles: What types of violations is SPIT targeting? Request DOB data on specific inspection outcomes.
Is the uptick tied to new construction wave or crackdown on existing violations?
